title: Habibsters Go Two for Two: Kaushal Repeats at Buckaroo Bowl II While Ben Dover Renews Its Lease on the Basement
dek: Kaushal turned an 11-3 season into a second straight title, Ramon crashed the final from the 3 seed, Randy's points crown went cold in December, and Sonny hit a 44.1-point rock bottom on the way to another last-place finish.
body: Year two of the Buckaroo Football League opened with six managers, a fresh draft, and one shared goal: knock Kaushal off the throne. By the end of the season, the throne had a second trophy sitting next to it. Habibsters won Buckaroo Bowl II, making Kaushal the only champion this league has ever known, and the other five managers spent December learning that dynasties don't care about your preseason optimism.

The regular season was all Habib. Habibsters went 11-3, the best record in the league by three full games, and scored 1524.8 points to lock up the No. 1 seed. That's a UGA-style season: win early, win often, and make the rest of the conference argue about second place. Behind him sat Randy's The fumblers at 8-6 as the 2 seed, Ramon's Araleasers at an even 7-7 as the 3 seed, and Alan's Team Pillbert sneaking in at 6-8 as the 4 seed.

Here's the number that will haunt Randy all offseason: The fumblers led the league with 1595.1 points, more than 70 ahead of the champion. Then the playoffs arrived and the offense went missing. Randy's team scored just 176.14 over the two-week semifinal, about 88 a week, and lost to Araleasers, who posted 202.44. The fumblers then finished fourth, behind a Team Pillbert squad that had a losing record, which is the kind of ending that should come with a complaint form.

Ramon's season was the biggest glow-up in the league. A year after posting the fewest points in 2023, Araleasers opened 2024 with a statement, dropping 166.58 in Week 1, the highest single-week score of the season. Brucie then hung around .500 all year, slid into the 3 seed, and knocked off the league's top scorer to reach the final. Not bad for a guy who wasn't sure he even wanted to join this thing.

On the other side of the bracket, Kaushal handled Alan 296.96 to 245.08 over two weeks, a 51-point gap that ended Philly's playoff run. Still, Team Pillbert deserves credit for squeezing a third-place finish out of a 6-8 record and 1473.9 points. Leave it to the league's favorite villain to lose more games than he won and still finish ahead of the team that scored the most points. Somewhere, Randy is still recalculating.

Buckaroo Bowl II was a blowout. Habibsters scored 261.44 to Araleasers' 145.28, a 116-point beatdown that turned the championship into a two-week victory lap. Ramon had a great ride to get there, but Kaushal was simply in a different gear, and the gap between first and second was wider than the gap between most teams' entire seasons. Two Bowls, two rings, zero mercy.

At the bottom, the consolation ladder delivered a sequel nobody requested. Sonny's Ben Dover went 5-9, scored a league-low 1304.3 points, and authored the season's worst afternoon with a 44.1 in Week 12, then finished last for the second straight year. Mekhi's Dawgs matched that 5-9 record but out-scored the commish by more than 100 points and escaped to fifth. And for the second year running, the league made zero trades, so every manager can say the same thing about their season: they did it all with their own roster. For Sonny, that's a rough read now, but every comeback story needs a basement to start from.
